changes.description: Retired. Decomposed into the three steps it was always made of. Its candidate narrowing -- evidence tier at or above a minimum, service matching -- is now a candidateFilter knob on nearest, which is honest as a knob by the test experiment 107 derived: it leaves both ports and the output carrier untouched and changes only which candidates are eligible. Its nearest-neighbour search was already shared code, merged into src/nearest-neighbour.ts earlier the same day. Its proxy-minutes derivation is now the travel_time primitive, a widget rather than a knob because a minutes column changes every row for every consumer, and deliberately not a third value of the unit knob because minutes is a model and not a unit -- a straight-line distance walked at a constant speed, which this widget's own method string already admitted. The filter conditions reproduce this widget's eligibility exactly, verified against the real Old Naledi data at 1 of 122 graded facilities. Not replaceable by a single widget, so a saved workflow holding this node cannot be migrated automatically: it must be rebuilt as nearest with a candidate filter, then travel_time, then the access-review ruleset at 2.0.0. The Old Naledi example was rewired that way in the same commit.

Names its replacement. The 0.2.0 retirement carried replacementCandidate forward as null from 0.1.0, and null is not a neutral value here: by this project's own rule it reads as NOT REPLACEABLE, which is the state that makes a saved workflow refuse to open rather than migrate. This widget is fully replaceable -- apply_ruleset declares a migrationFrom adapter for it at src/core.ts#validateWorkflow, pinning the ruleset at the version that produced this widget's results -- so the field said the opposite of what the adapter does. Found by building the retired-widget lookup in docs/usage.md, which is what reading a declared field rather than the prose beside it is for.
First registry snapshot of existing behavior; no implementation change or historical version reconstruction.

One widget for every declared ruleset, replacing policy, access_policy and xpert, which differed only in which rules they ran. All three carried their rules as template literals inside their executors while policy described itself as 'Apply N3 rules with EYE-JS', as though rules were an input; they were not. The rules became declared, versioned, digested artefacts earlier on 2026-10-12 with byte-identical output, and this is the node type that hosts them. What this merge does: it collapses three palette entries to one and three widget contracts to one. What it does not do: collapse the three projections. Each ruleset still assembles a different carrier for whatever consumes it, and that code is dispatched here by declared data rather than deleted -- a merge that claimed to remove code and only moved it would be worse than no merge. A saved workflow holding any of the three is rewritten with its ruleset pinned at the version that produced its results, and stamped so the Inspector names the replacement. Ports are declared empty here and pinned per node from the ruleset, which is exactly how micro_workflow declares a composition's: src/core.ts nodeInputs and outputOf already vary per node, so this reuses the mechanism compositions established rather than inventing one.

Renamed from `area` to `study_area`. The old identifier keeps resolving: a saved workflow naming `area` is rewritten on open and stamped with sourceMigration, because the operation is unchanged and a rename must not refuse work the way a retirement does. `area` is a category noun -- which area? It is the study area, and the widget's own title has said "Study area" all along, so the type and the title disagreed. The port type and the port name stay `area`: a port carrying a study area is still an area, and a rename changes a node type, never a port. No contract change: ports, output, parameters and behaviour are identical.
Add dimensioned square and rectangular bounding boxes; persisted CRS84 geometry and existing polygons are unchanged.
Reusable local catchment primitive; see docs/experiments/32-john-snow-primitives.md. Bounded prototype, not an exact notebook replay.

Defines a study area as everything within a stated distance of one named point, which previously existed only welded inside Select nearby facilities. One named point only: the bounding box of several distant points makes a raster window too coarse to sample, measured as a 1,469 m cell across three Philippine gauges against 19 m for one 5 km scope. Refuses an unknown or unlocated point and never unions several.

Counts cases per day, week or month from a declared date attribute and a declared kind of date, optionally weighted by an attribute where one record stands for several cases. Zero-count periods are retained and records without an ISO 8601 date are excluded and counted. The first widget on the time axis; see docs/experiments/61-input-dimensions.md.

Retired. Superseded by observations, exactly as places is: the same adapter in src/core.ts#validateWorkflow migrates every saved centers node, keeping its label, records and connections, and stamps sourceMigration so the Inspector names the replacement. One worked example's cooling centres, declared 'example-specific' by this widget about itself.

Pins the renderers. fw:chartRendererVersion has been written into receipts since the Vega-Lite prototype, but the widget metadata said nothing about the engine, so a release digest could stay identical while the library that draws every figure changed underneath it. scripts/validate-widgets.mjs now checks the pinned libraries against package.json and the declared default against chartRenderer(), so bumping vega-lite forces a new release. Records vega-lite as the default, changed the same day.

Adds a case-series mode: a Chart output connected to Cases by period draws an epidemic curve, with the period on the axis and the kind of date stated in the caption. A presentation of the series with no smoothing and no interpolation.

bandMeasure: 'difference' charts the difference between neighbouring nested bands instead of their cumulative counts, and does it with a Vega-Lite window/calculate transform in the specification rather than arithmetic in the application. Nested travel-time bands give cumulative counts -- a location one minute from a pump is inside all four rings -- while the case study's own bar chart subtracts as it walks outward (Advanced-1 NB04 cell 19). A prototype that deliberately departs from the house style of charting already computed bins: the whole spec is recorded as fw:rendererSpecification, so a declared transform is more inspectable in the provenance than the same subtraction in TypeScript. It requires the Vega-Lite renderer, renames the measure, says so in the caption, keeps the cumulative count in the tooltip, and asserts a distinct fw:chartMeasureKind of band-difference-of-<kind> with unit status location-memberships-differenced-between-bands. Refused unless every bin carries a distinct travel time and the counts actually increase outward, which proves nesting from the data rather than assuming it. See docs/experiments/87-declarative-chart-transforms.md.
Reusable local catchment primitive; see docs/experiments/32-john-snow-primitives.md. Bounded prototype, not an exact notebook replay.

Align the all-touched inclusion rule with GDAL ALL_TOUCHED, measured cell by cell against rasterio 1.5.2 and GDAL 3.12.2 in the Validation Lab: differences over a deliberately pixel-aligned cutline fall from 35 cells to 2, and the cropped window now agrees. The residual 2 cells come from GDAL burning cells along a cutline vertex lying exactly on a cell border, which is an artifact of its line rasterizer rather than a stateable rule. Records the convention and the outer margin in N3 evidence. See docs/experiments/29-raster-edge-inclusion.md.

Migration, no adapter required: All touched now includes a cell only when the cutline covers part of its area or crosses its interior. A cutline edge lying exactly on the border between two cells no longer pulls in the cell outside it, and the cropped window is no longer padded. Re-running a saved all-touched clip can therefore retain fewer boundary cells, and any total derived from one can change. Cell center inside is unaffected. Receipts from earlier runs carry no fw:rasterMaskConvention and were produced by the more inclusive rule.
Unweighted mean-center evaluation with shared pump context; see docs/experiments/35-cholera-geoprivacy-workflow.md.
Explicit typed Mean center inputs on both branches; legacy three-input comparisons remain supported.
Unweighted mean-center evaluation with shared pump context; see docs/experiments/35-cholera-geoprivacy-workflow.md.
First registry snapshot of existing behavior; no implementation change or historical version reconstruction.
Bounded geoprivacy worked example; see docs/experiments/35-cholera-geoprivacy-workflow.md.

Separate historical registry into shared Input data and connected radius selection. Legacy nodes without sourceMode receive a source and connector once; existing selection IDs, settings and outgoing connections remain. Computation receipt and source lineage are retained.

Consumes a general point layer instead of the gradedFacilities carrier, and the port is named for what it carries rather than for the widget that used to produce it. gradedFacilities was a producer-named stud -- D4a is the criterion -- emitted by one widget and consumed by two, and retiring it is what let nearest take the graded facilities as candidates and filter on tier and service with its own knob, which is what decomposing access needed. What a point layer cannot carry is the registry boundary and facilitySource that the old carrier passed through here; those belong to the nodes that produced them, and a consumer reaching through a carrier to find them is how a thin carrier becomes a thick one. Neither is used by the table this widget feeds, which is what makes the loss safe rather than merely acceptable.

Each polygon replaced by its outer ring, so enclosed gaps become solid. This is isochrone's fillHoles as a step of its own, and it is what Advanced-1 NB03 does: Polygon(new_iso.exterior) at cell 64, the definition that produced the shapefiles NB04 reads. Cell 94 redefines the function to take a convex hull of multipart results and never calls it, which had earlier been mistaken for the operative infill. Takes no UTM zone, unlike the nine widgets that do: the input states the metric CRS its upstream used and this reads it, because a zone asked for twice can be answered twice. Gaps between separate polygons are untouched -- it fills enclosed space and does not join things up. The dangerous case governs itself through the port type: donut_geomask, where a hole is the privacy mechanism, emits points and cannot reach a polygons input. See docs/experiments/88-filling-interior-gaps.md.

One operation, two sources, both reachable from a browser with no account. Measured 2026-10-09: Overpass answers with access-control-allow-origin: * and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team country export on HDX is served from S3 with the same header, 452 KB compressed for 12,776 Philippine facilities of which 11,877 are named. The study area bounds the query rather than filtering it afterwards, so the area is the scope of the question; the country export is clipped to that area because it is not bounded at source, while the live query is not clipped again because doing so would only mask a bounding-box error. Both sources are OpenStreetMap-derived and both are ODbL. Retrieval happens in the interface and never in the executor, so a workflow runs from stored data with the network off; core.ts imports the value and validation functions from this module and deliberately not the download function. Supersedes healthsites_discovery, which was excluded because healthsites.io sends no cross-origin header and could not be fetched at all; see docs/experiments/69-healthsites-acquisition.md and 71-health-facility-sources.md.

0.2.0 adds Overture Maps Places as a third source, read directly from GeoParquet on S3. It is the first source here that is not OpenStreetMap-derived, so it can corroborate rather than echo; it is CDLA Permissive 2.0 rather than share-alike; and it states a confidence for each place, which is the only numeric quality signal any of these sources offer. Measured 2026-10-10 against release 2026-09-23.1: 16 parts, 4,864 row groups, 81,455,423 rows, 11.0 GB, of which a Manila study area selected 3 row groups in 1 part, 55,649 rows, read in about 1.5 seconds; the 16 footers are read concurrently because sequentially they took 22 seconds. The release is discovered rather than pinned and recorded in the receipt, so a default that moves does not make a past run unreadable. A truncated bucket listing is refused rather than silently dropping files, because a missing file looks like an empty study area and an empty study area looks like a true absence. Overture's bbox columns are 32-bit and bracket the coordinate rather than equal it (measured: only 0.12% degenerate), so they select row groups and the geometry supplies the coordinates. Overture's categories are mapped onto this application's facility kinds as a declared equivalence, deliberately conservative: the generic buckets health_care, medical_service and specialized_health_care are not mapped at all, because measured in a Manila study area they carried a wellness spa, individually named doctors and a training course, and Overture reported 207 places under hospital where a live OpenStreetMap query returned 47 hospitals and clinics together. Counts from this source are not comparable with the OpenStreetMap sources and the receipt says so. See docs/experiments/71-health-facility-sources.md.

Renamed from `hex_aggregate` to `aggregate_points_to_h3_cell`. The old identifier keeps resolving: a saved workflow naming `hex_aggregate` is rewritten on open and stamped with sourceMigration, because the operation is unchanged and a rename must not refuse work the way a retirement does. The verb came after its object and the areal unit was unstated, while its sibling said verb first. Both now read as one operation over a named unit: aggregate points to H3 cells. The unit is the ontology's own term (fw:HexCell, 'H3 cell'), not 'hexbin', because a plotting library's hexbin is a lattice fitted to its data and these cells come from a fixed global index. No contract change: ports, output, parameters and behaviour are identical.

Retitled from "Group points in H3 cells". The node type names hexagonal aggregation and the title named the indexing method instead, so the two shared no word and a reader had to know that H3 cells are hexagons to connect them. Flagged by the naming ratchet added 2026-10-13 under title-type-agreement; the convention's own rule is that the node type and the title must say the same thing. No contract change: ports, output, parameters and behaviour are identical, which is why this is a patch.
Bounded geoprivacy worked example; see docs/experiments/35-cholera-geoprivacy-workflow.md.
Optional bounded list of cumulative time thresholds and explicit interior-hole infill; preserves single-time corridor defaults.

All three segments of a walk are now charged and drawn. The walk onto the network comes out of the budget; the walk off it at the end is the leg the budget still allows up to bufferM, so the region ends at its own time rather than bufferM beyond it; and the region is the whole route buffered rather than the streets alone. A site beyond the snap limit is routed anyway and marked off-network instead of ending the run, and one whose walk alone spends the budget gets no catchment and is named. Results change: the John Snow bands shrink by 39.3%, 13.8%, 4.2% and 0%, and the one-minute band holds 21 locations and 65 deaths where it held 48 and 110. Experiment 114.

A map declares every layer port it can draw and the practitioner wires what they have. The inputMode parameter no longer decides which ports exist, which presentation is offered or whether a basemap can be chosen; the renderer is read from the connections. The practitioner's direction of 2026-10-14 -- "there is no such thing as mode, only layers" -- which had been written into docs/widgets/map_output.md and into the layer vocabulary of the receipts while the interface kept asking the question.
changes.migration: None required for a saved workflow. The stored inputMode is read last and never written.

changes.description: Optional weightField: each point is weighted by a named record attribute, with the field and the weight total asserted in the receipt beside the unchanged point count. Unweighted when no field is given.
First registry snapshot of existing behavior; no implementation change or historical version reconstruction.

A composition used as one step. One node type serves every composition: the node pins the composition's id, version, title, stage, ports and output type, so nodeInputs and outputOf read the contract from the node rather than the type table, and a saved workflow validates and reports drift without the composition file being present. Runs by expansion after the authored workflow is validated, so the executor has no composition branch and one receipt per member falls out of running ordinary nodes. Not addable from the palette yet: the palette offers admitted compositions, and none is admitted. Its params are the first thing in a saved workflow to record a version, against the not-yet-persisted claim every other release makes -- which is deliberate, because without a version there is nothing for drift detection to check when the file is reopened.

Records the arrangement. 0.1.0 declared an ontology gap: the node expanded before execution and emitted nothing, so a run showed four member activities with nothing saying they came from one composition at one version. Now the expansion emits a PROV association rather than invented vocabulary -- the composition is a prov:Plan and each member is associated with it -- and the members' receipts are unchanged, which is the other half of the requirement: a run of a composition must read as a run of the primitives. Also makes the node addable: the palette offers one entry per bundled composition with its governance status on the entry, replacing the reading that only an admitted composition may be added at all. That reading gated trying on review, and so gated the learning the review exists to protect.

Renamed from `nearest` to `measure_distance`. The old identifier keeps resolving: a saved workflow naming `nearest` is rewritten on open and stamped with sourceMigration, because the operation is unchanged and a rename must not refuse work the way a retirement does. `nearest` is a bare adjective, which the naming convention refuses: it names a property of the answer rather than the operation, and the operation is measuring the distance to the closest candidate. No contract change: ports, output, parameters and behaviour are identical.

A candidate filter, which is what `access` added over this widget. Held as a KNOB rather than built as a widget, by the test experiment 107 derived the same day: a knob is honest when the contract does not move with it. This leaves both ports and the output carrier untouched and changes only which candidates are eligible, which is what a threshold does too. Its language is experiment 106's authored condition -- a field, a comparator, a value -- so the rule builder's form now serves a third caller, after classification and the role binding experiment 61 proposes.

The comparators are `in` and `notIn` over a declared set, deliberately, and not an ordinal `>=`. Old Naledi asks for 'evidence at least Contextual', an ordinal comparison on a categorical, and over a finite declared vocabulary that compiles to the set {Direct, Contextual} -- the same move by which OR compiles to one rule per disjunct. An authoring surface may offer 'at least Contextual'; what is stored and executed is the set.

A candidate missing the attribute a condition names FAILS the condition rather than passing it: an unrecorded evidence level has not met a minimum evidence level, and the looser reading would quietly widen the search.

The filter's two counts -- how many candidates were located and how many survived narrowing -- are reported in this widget's own receipt and method string, so the exclusion and the search cannot disagree about what was considered. That is what holding the filter here buys over a separate node, and the note on when a node would earn its place instead is in docs/experiments/103-duplicates-should-merge.md.

Verified against the real Old Naledi data: the knob's conditions select the identical eligible set to `access`'s own predicate, 1 of 122 graded facilities. This does not yet retire `access`, which also derives proxy minutes and receives its candidates on the gradedFacilities carrier.

Downloads are judged on what they cost rather than on how wide the area is: the fixed 6 km envelope is gone, and the byte and feature limits are their own numbers instead of following the isochrone graph limit. The default graph size is 50,000 network nodes, which admits a real town. Each instance's /api/status is read before downloading -- free slots, rate limit, and when the next slot frees -- and a busy service is waited for rather than treated as a failure. Responses are kept on the device and reused for the same query; pressing Download again when a network is already saved fetches a fresh one. The widget shows endpoint status before a download, progress on the button while it runs, which instance served the saved graph, and why a download failed.
Reusable local catchment primitive; see docs/experiments/32-john-snow-primitives.md. Bounded prototype, not an exact notebook replay.

Renamed from `observations` to `point_input`. The old identifier keeps resolving: a saved workflow naming `observations` is rewritten on open and stamped with sourceMigration, because the operation is unchanged and a rename must not refuse work the way a retirement does. `observations` is a category noun, and the title "Input data" said "input" where the identifier did not and shared no word with it -- so a reader had to learn a mapping that carried no information. The operation is importing observed points, and the title is now "Point data", which matches `table_input` and "Tabular data". Clears three violations: audited-name, role-word-in-title and title-type-agreement. No contract change: ports, output, parameters and behaviour are identical.
Heat examples use shared input editing. Legacy places and centers normalize on load without changing IDs, labels, references, geometry or scalar attributes; sourceMigration records adapter version 1.

Retired. Superseded by map_output, table_output and chart_output, which this widget's own 0.1.2 note already recorded -- it was removed from the palette and kept as an import compatibility identity. What changed on 2026-10-12 is that the declaration now has an effect: implementationStatus 'retired' had been a permitted value since this format was written and no file in src/ read it, so src/palette.ts carried a hand-typed array instead and the widget still held a row in the counts. src/palette.ts now derives retirement from this field. A retired widget never runs: src/output-contract.ts#migrateOutputNodes rewrites every saved output node to the output type matching the view it saved, and stamps sourceMigration so the Inspector names the replacement rather than rewriting the practitioner's work in silence. Fully replaceable, so no saved workflow refuses to open.

Retired. Superseded by observations, which this widget already declared as its replacementCandidate and which src/core.ts#validateWorkflow has migrated every saved places node into since adapter version 1 -- the node keeps its label, records and connections and is stamped sourceMigration so the Inspector says so. The widget's own release note already called it 'a legacy loading alias'; what changed on 2026-10-12 is that implementationStatus 'retired' is read, so the alias leaves the palette, the counts and the coverage ledger instead of sitting in them. It declared standardization 'example-specific' about itself -- one worked example's neighbourhoods -- which under the rule that no widget may be name-attached to a worked example is a self-reported failed admission.

Distinguish reading a retained raster window at execution from acquiring the source asset.

Divides counted events by a declared population at risk, grouping by an attribute or by bands of a numeric one. The denominator's unit, the kind of rate, the multiplier, the smallest reportable denominator and both vintages are declared rather than implied. See docs/research/john-snow-data-sets.md for the data that motivated it.

The second half of isochrone: walks each street leaving a reached junction as far as the budget left there allows, and buffers the result. Fifth of six primitives an isochrone composition needs, and the one that makes the chain produce a polygon. Restates nothing -- remainingM and travelDirection arrive on the junctions, so the corridor cannot disagree with the traversal that produced them, and junctions from two traversals are refused rather than mixed. Extracting it moved the edge-orientation check and the part-way truncation into src/network-edges.ts, which isochrone now imports too, so the 2 metre endpoint tolerance exists once rather than twice. Takes a UTM zone because buffering in degrees is wrong, which makes nine widgets that each ask for one. See docs/experiments/84-reachable-corridor.md.

A corridor drawn from banded junctions now carries that band's minutes on the polygon, names the feature by it, and says in its notes that a band's corridor contains every shorter band's. Junctions from more than one band in a single corridor are refused, since one polygon cannot stand for two travel times. The minutes attribute already travels into receipts as fw:travelTimeMinutes, which isochrone has always set. Additive: unbanded input behaves as before.

The corridor is the whole route buffered, and the buffer is charged. The walk off the street at the end of a route is now min(bufferM, the budget left at that point), so the corridor is full width while there is time to spare and tapers to nothing where the time runs out, instead of claiming bufferM of ground beyond the budget all the way round its boundary. When the junctions carry the origin’s location, the straight first leg from the site is part of the corridor too. bufferM therefore means the furthest anyone is assumed to walk off a street, not a drawing width. Measured on the John Snow five-minute band: 186,035 m² to 160,415 m². Experiment 114.

Street junctions within a travel budget of an origin, each carrying the budget left on arrival. Extracted from the Dijkstra inside isochrone (src/catchments.ts:76) unchanged, including the edge reversal that makes inbound a different question from outbound. Fourth of six primitives an isochrone composition needs. Settles the question that stopped the decomposition in experiment 82 -- what a reached junction travels as: the truncation downstream consumes budget minus cost at the edge's start node, which is a per-node quantity, so reached junctions travel as points with a remainingM attribute and no lines port type is needed. The corridor step that follows truncates by remainingM over lengthM and never restates the minutes or the speed. Takes no UTM zone, unlike the eight metric widgets: costs are the network's own lengthM values and nothing here re-measures geometry. Travel mode is an explicit parameter -- walking, cycling, driving or other -- checked against the speed, because the 75 metres per minute this project defaulted to everywhere is 4.5 km/h from Advanced-1 NB03 cell 10, where it is an assumption about pedestrians in Soho in 1854 and was being inherited rather than chosen. Public transport is refused as a mode, because it follows routes and a timetable rather than the street network. See docs/experiments/83-reachable-junctions.md.

Each reached junction now carries travelDirection beside remainingM. The corridor step that follows has to truncate edges the same way round as the traversal ran, and direction was a parameter of this node that its output did not state -- so the corridor would have needed its own direction parameter, free to contradict this one. Carrying it as data closes that, for the same reason remainingM is carried rather than the budget. Additive: no existing attribute changed.

Each reached junction now carries speedMPerMin and travelMode. travel_time_band has to convert its minutes into metres, and the speed was a parameter of this node that its output did not state -- so the band would have needed its own speed parameter, free to contradict this one, which is the defect the mode plausibility bands exist to catch. Carrying it as data closes it, for the same reason remainingM and travelDirection are carried. Additive: no existing attribute changed.

The walk from the site onto the network is charged against the budget. It was measured, attached to the point and then spent by nothing, so every reachable set reached further than its time allowed. An origin whose walk alone spends the budget now reaches nothing and is reported rather than silently returning an empty set. Junctions also carry the origin’s own coordinates and its snap distance, so whatever draws a corridor can draw the first leg of the route. Experiment 114.

Attaches its own origins. It refused any point without a networkNodeId and named snap_to_network as the fix, which made a whole widget a prerequisite for one nearest-neighbour search; it now finds the junction itself, by the same nearestNetworkNode over the same projection that widget uses, so the two paths agree junction for junction and metre for metre. A point arriving already snapped is used exactly as it arrives and nothing is projected. Three parameters are therefore declared -- zone, hemisphere and maxSnapM -- and all three are OPTIONAL, because this widget's reason for having no zone stays true whenever origins arrive snapped: nothing in the Dijkstra re-measures geometry, so a run that attaches nothing has nothing to project and is not asked for a frame. Completeness is refused at run time, naming the origins that needed it, which is why no saved workflow had to be migrated and no zone had to be invented for one. Unlike snap_to_network this does NOT move the point: it reads the nearest junction, charges the distance against the budget and leaves the origin where it stands. Additive -- every workflow that ran against 0.4.0 runs unchanged. Step 1 and 2 of the snap_to_network retirement; see docs/experiments/82-snap-to-network.md.
Split: the widget stopped importing its own data and became a points-to-points transform, projecting CRS84 into a UTM zone.
changes.migration: A node saved under 0.1.0 carries params.data holding points the old widget had ALREADY converted to CRS84 at import. validateWorkflow rewrites such a node to point_input with those records, its label and its connections kept, and stamps sourceMigration.fromType 'reproject'. Recorded as a RecontractedNodeType: the type was neither retired nor renamed, its contract changed.

changes.description: Import-time projection change from WGS84 UTM metres to CRS84 degrees; see docs/experiments/40-reprojection-primitives.md. WGS84 zones only, no datum shift, no raster warping. Narrower than the general Reproject node proposed in experiment 05.

Writes the value of the raster cell containing each point onto that point, under PixelIsArea with no interpolation. Closes the gap experiment 62 found: the elevation attribute Compare level to elevation requires could not be produced in the application at all. No-data cells, points outside the raster and points without coordinates carry no value and are counted separately; none is zero-filled. An attribute already present on the layer is refused rather than overwritten, and a raster on another CRS is refused because no datum shift exists.

Renamed from `samples` to `point_grid`. The old identifier keeps resolving: a saved workflow naming `samples` is rewritten on open and stamped with sourceMigration, because the operation is unchanged and a rename must not refuse work the way a retirement does. `samples` named the content of one demonstration rather than the operation, and this widget's own title had said "Point grid" all along, so the type and the title disagreed -- which the naming convention forbids. Flagged by the ratchet added 2026-10-13 under audited-name and title-type-agreement; this clears both. No contract change: ports, output, parameters and behaviour are identical.

Generalised in place. The computation was always general -- a bounding extent, a metre spacing converted to degrees at the extent's mid-latitude, and an even-odd containment test -- but the widget declared itself example-specific and earned it three ways: it was titled 'Sample locations', described as generating 'demonstration points', and defined inside one worked example's module in OLD_TYPES. It also stamped samplingBasis 'demonstration-grid' onto every point it produced, which is a claim about a demonstration rather than about a grid. The operation now lives in src/point-grid.ts with no default geometry, the title is 'Point grid', the stamp reads 'regular-grid', and the widget is on the shared palette instead of one example's template. No new node type and no migration: a saved workflow holding this node loads unchanged and no example's node count moves. The spacing range check moved to src/core.ts with it, because validateOldNode only runs for OLD_TYPES members and leaving it behind would have silently stopped enforcing 150-1000 m.

Declares an imported long-format table as a bounded extract of published AR6 projections, requiring the full key, metre units, the dataset and version, the baseline period, three obligatory citations and which family value includes vertical land motion. Imports and declares; acquires nothing and produces no projection.
Nearest published site per point by straight-line distance, with the distance retained as part of the result and points without coordinates kept and reported as unassigned.

Compares one fully keyed projected change against a practitioner-supplied elevation on a stated vertical datum, classifying each point as reaching, staying below, or unknown. Refuses to run without a datum, without a named elevation attribute, or with a partial key.

Attaches each site to its nearest network node, measured in metres, and carries how far it moved as a snapDistanceM attribute on the point. Extracted from isochrone, which snaps inside itself and then states in a note that the distance is reported but not charged; on a node of its own that admission is visible and mappable. Third of six primitives an isochrone composition needs, and the first taken from the source end: building backwards stopped because reached edges are truncated mid-street and validateNetwork requires every edge endpoint to be a declared node, so no existing carrier can hold them. Takes a UTM zone to measure a distance, which makes eight widgets that each ask for one. See docs/experiments/82-snap-to-network.md.

A site beyond the snap limit is no longer refused. It is snapped anyway and marked: the point carries offNetworkMetres as well as snapDistanceM, and the activity asserts fw:offNetworkSiteCount and fw:offNetworkSites. Refusing removed exactly the sites furthest from a mapped road, which is where street data is thinnest and where an access question is most often asked. The widget also keeps each site’s own coordinates on the point it moves, as siteLongitude and siteLatitude: it kept only the distance, so nothing downstream could draw or undo the displacement. Experiment 114.

Gathers up to six polygon layers into one with nothing merged, ordered largest area first so smaller polygons draw on top. Needed because the isochrone rings arrive as one corridor per band and every output node takes a single polygons input: unioning them with summarize_combined_area would give one blob the size of the largest band with the walking times gone. Numbered ports follow the point-layer convention in src/point-layers.ts, capped at six because isochrone accepts at most six thresholds. Takes no UTM zone: ring extent in degrees decides draw order and is never reported, so there is no area to get wrong. Refuses layers computed in different coordinate systems, and refuses polygons sharing an identifier, which could not be told apart once collected.

Overlapping and touching areas become one; separate areas stay separate. GIS calls it dissolve. Derived from the isochrone decomposition: Advanced-1 NB03 buffers the reachable segments, hulls them, then unions the result, and Fieldwork's isochrone already calls polygonClipping.union inside itself to fill holes, so the operation was in the codebase and never a widget. Second of six primitives an isochrone composition needs, taken second because the decomposition is built backwards from its output: summarize_hull emits polygons, which is what this takes. Takes a UTM zone to report an area, which makes seven widgets that each ask for one. See docs/experiments/81-combined-area.md.

The smallest convex outline containing a set of points, computed in a metric CRS. Derived from the PHI case studies rather than proposed: Advanced-2 NB02 hulls its death locations to bound a Voronoi diagram and Advanced-1 NB03 hulls the reached network, and docs/research/john-snow-voronoi.md recorded that hull and buffer should not be hidden inside Voronoi. It is also the first of six primitives an isochrone composition needs, and the only one unblocked today. Refuses fewer than three located points and refuses collinear ones, because a line encloses nothing. Takes a UTM zone for the same reason five other widgets do — a layer cannot state the coordinate system it is in, which is D5's finding in experiment 40 and this makes six. Named with a stage verb under the taxonomy proposed in experiment 76: many points become one shape, which is summarising. See docs/experiments/80-convex-hull.md.

Renamed from `summarize_polygons` to `summarize_points_to_polygon`. The old identifier keeps resolving: a saved workflow naming `summarize_polygons` is rewritten on open and stamped with sourceMigration, because the operation is unchanged and a rename must not refuse work the way a retirement does. The node type named its grouping as if it were the object: the operation reduces POINTS, and the polygons are the areal units it reduces them to. summarize_combined_area is the widget that genuinely summarizes polygons. No contract change: ports, output, parameters and behaviour are identical.
Reusable local catchment primitive; see docs/experiments/32-john-snow-primitives.md. Bounded prototype, not an exact notebook replay.

Long-format tabular import with declared key and value columns, an author-stated unit and rejection of duplicate key tuples. Closes the host gap that blocked the sea-level pack; see docs/experiments/48-tabular-input.md.

Accept a keyed data table as an input mode, displaying its key columns and value. Saved workflows keep their existing mode and need no migration. Chart and Map deliberately do not accept a table: charting one requires choosing which key varies and whether to aggregate, which is a design decision rather than a rendering detail.

Extracted from the retired access widget, which derived proxy minutes inside a nearest-neighbour search. A widget and not a knob on nearest, by the test experiment 107 derived: a minutes column changes every row for every consumer of the distances carrier, so the contract moves. And not a third value of the unit knob either -- metres to kilometres is a pure conversion while minutes is a MODEL, a straight-line distance walked at a constant speed, and putting a model behind a unit selector would present an assumption as a unit. The assumption is named in the receipt on every run. Reads each row unit rather than assuming kilometres, because a metre reading divided by metres-per-minute is right while a kilometre reading is wrong by a thousand. A row with no distance gains no minutes: a missing distance is not a travel time of zero.

Narrows reachable junctions to a shorter travel time, recomputing the budget left at each against the band. The rings of an isochrone map -- 1, 5, 10 and 15 minutes in the case study -- are not four traversals: a cumulative band is a subset, and the notebook's own note says nested thresholds are cumulative rather than disjoint. isochrone recomputes the whole Dijkstra per threshold including the snap, four times over for the Soho example, where one traversal banded four ways gives the same answer. Not a generic attribute filter, and deliberately: reachable_corridor truncates streets by remainingM over lengthM, so keeping a five minute subset of a fifteen minute traversal without recomputing remainingM would leave the longer budget's leftovers in place and draw corridors past the band, silently. The filter and the recomputation have to happen together. Takes no zone and no speed: the speed arrives on the junctions and the traversal's budget is recovered from them.

Each junction kept now carries bandMinutes. reachable_corridor reads it to stamp the band's travel time onto the polygon it draws, so a map can colour by walking time and a chart can label by it, as the case study's outputs do. Without it the four rings arrive at a map indistinguishable from one another. Additive: no existing attribute changed.

Records the fw: terms this widget asserts, as ontology.emits, derived from its module by scripts/ontology-coupling.mjs. The point is the coupling rather than the list: the terms a widget asserts can no longer change without a new release, so a composition pinning the old one reports drift, and ontology drift and widget drift become one signal. Declares 1 class and 6 properties. No behaviour change.
Reusable local catchment primitive; see docs/experiments/32-john-snow-primitives.md. Bounded prototype, not an exact notebook replay.

Names its replacement. The 0.2.0 retirement carried replacementCandidate forward as null from 0.1.0, and null is not a neutral value here: by this project's own rule it reads as NOT REPLACEABLE, which is the state that makes a saved workflow refuse to open rather than migrate. This widget is fully replaceable -- apply_ruleset declares a migrationFrom adapter for it at src/core.ts#validateWorkflow, pinning the ruleset at the version that produced this widget's results -- so the field said the opposite of what the adapter does. Found by building the retired-widget lookup in docs/usage.md, which is what reading a declared field rather than the prose beside it is for.
